newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's MGTS may issue Eurobond in Q2 97.
newsitem.headline: Russia's MGTS may issue Eurobond in Q2 97.

text.p: Moscow City Telephone (MGTS) may issue a privately placed Eurobond in the second quarter of 1997, a senior MGTS official said on Wednesday.

Boris Lastovich, head of the securities department at OAO Moskovskaya Gorodskaya Telefonnaya Set (MGTS), told Reuters the company was having talks with U.S. investment bank Salomon Bros about making an issue under the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission's (SEC) rule 144a governing private placements.
"If everything is in order, we will be able to issue the securities most likely at the beginning of the second quarter of next year," he said.
MGTS is not considering issuing American Depositary Receipts (ADRs), as several other Russian companies have done, he said.
Most of these issues have been level-one ADRs, allowing foreign investors to trade the Russian company's shares while avoiding domestic settlement problems, but not raising capital for the issuer.
To raise capital, a company must issue level-three ADRs, for which the SEC lays down stricter reporting rules.
Lastovich noted that another Russian telecoms group, privately owned Vimpel-Communications, had recently made a successful issue of level-three ADRs in New York.
But he said it would be much more difficult for a partly privatised company such as MGTS to issue level-three ADRs.
Lastovich said MGTS's 1996 figures would probably be audited by Coopers & Lybrand, which audited its 1995 results.
State telecoms holding company OAO Investitsionnaya Kompaniya Svyazi (Svyazinvest) holds 46.7 percent of the voting shares on 35 percent of the capital of MGTS.

As of April 1, the Moscow Committee for Science and Technology held 33 percent of the voting shares, Bank of Bermuda 3.37 percent, Russian financial company Guta-Invest 1.01 percent, CS First Boston 1.23 percent and Burlington Investments 1.28 percent.
Salomon Bros won a tender in July to lead an offering of MGTS Eurobonds. It handled a private placement of ADRs for Moscow power company Mosenergo in October last year.
At 1145 GMT Mosenergo had not been traded on the Russian Trading System on Wednesday. It was quoted at $720/$775 against $720/$825 on Tuesday. It last traded on Friday at $800.
